problem: The statement "If not, I_xy≠0 and the axes are not principal" is wrong as a general rule. A layout that is not symmetric about both centroidal axes can still give I_xy = 0: symmetry about even one centroidal axis is enough, because every boom at (x, y) has a partner at (−x, y) or (x, −y), so ΣA x y cancels. In that case the centroidal axes are still principal axes.
fix: "If the booms are symmetric about both centroidal axes, I_xy = 0. So is the case with symmetry about one axis only, since the boom pairs then cancel ΣA x y. I_xy is non-zero only when the layout has no such symmetry; then the centroidal axes are not principal and must be rotated by the standard principal-axis formula."

problem: The positive sense of M_x and M_y is never defined, so a student cannot tell which way the neutral axis tilts or how to sign the moments taken from Unit 1. The worked example uses a convention (positive M_x gives tension at positive y, positive M_y gives tension at positive x) without saying so.
fix: State the convention before the formula: "Take M_x positive when it produces tension at positive y, and M_y positive when it produces tension at positive x. Then σ = M_x y/I_xx + M_y x/I_yy."

problem: "the skin's direct area moves the axis and tilts every stress" is unclear — stress is not tilted.
fix: "Using the centroid of the skin outline instead of the centroid of the boom areas puts the reference axes in the wrong place; this changes I_xx, I_yy and I_xy and therefore changes every boom stress."

problem: The answer names the coupling terms but does not say what coupling means, so a student can reproduce the symbols without understanding them.
fix: "With I_xy≠0 each moment acts on both coordinates: M_x produces stress varying with x through the −M_x I_xy x term and M_y produces stress varying with y through the −M_y I_xy y term. That is what couples M_x and M_y."
